messages:
Samir V: Heads-up: demo run this morning revealed inconsistent error shapes across SDKs. Android returns {message: string}, node returns an object with `error_code`, python raises RuntimeError with no metadata. The onboarding sample crashed when it tried to inspect `.status`.

Lina Gomez: Oh no. This is probably fallout from the auth/backoff refactor. We promised typed exceptions for DX parity, but looks like the mappings never landed consistently.

Ethan Wu: Quick checklist: 1) canonical envelope keys, 2) SDK-level typed exceptions, 3) boolean `retryable` or machine-friendly hint, 4) `retry_after` when applicable. If we have that, sample apps and UI can behave deterministically.

Samir V: Agreed. Proposed canonical envelope: top-level `error` object with keys: `code` (string, machine id), `status` (int HTTP), `message` (string for humans), `retryable` (bool), `retry_after` (int seconds, optional), `docs` (url). Put minimal example in spec so SDKs copy it.

Lina Gomez: Example to paste into each SDK test: 

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "auth_invalid_token",
    "status": 401,
    "message": "Access token expired",
    "retryable": false,
    "docs": "https://docs.redwood.ai/errors#auth_invalid_token"
  }
}
```

Ethan Wu: For 5xx we should default to `TransientError` with `retryable=true`. For 429 specifically surface `RateLimitError` and include `retry_after` whenever gateway supplies `Retry-After` header.

Samir V: Edge cases: custom gateway statuses (e.g., 430) should not derp SDK mappings. Suggest fallback rule: if envelope present, honor `retryable` flag. If envelope absent, map by status class: 5xx -> TransientError (retryable), 429 -> RateLimitError, 401/403 -> AuthError (non-retryable by default).

Lina Gomez: We'll also need to add small integration tests in the onboarding sample that assert the SDK throws a typed exception with attributes: `.code`, `.status`, `.retryable`, `.retry_after` (optional). QA Bot: can add a smoke job to CI to run the sample against a stubbed error gateway.

QA Bot: Creating a CI smoke test ticket now and will include a minimal harness that returns the example envelope + varied headers. ETA for test job: 48h.

Ethan Wu: Ownership and plan: Lina updates the error spec and adds example (2 days). Samir patches node + python SDK to unify envelope parsing and typed exceptions (5 days). I'll handle Android mapping (3 days). We'll coordinate via three PRs and link a test in each.

Lina Gomez: Also proposal for logs/telemetry: emit `error.code` tag (string) and `error.retryable` boolean so we can alert on auth_error spikes vs rate limits. Add it to SDK telemetry hooks.

Samir V: One more nuance: token refresh flows. Some 401s are recoverable by refresh; SDKs should expose an `AuthError` with `.can_refresh = true/false` when known. Do not silently retry unless SDK has built-in refresh and caller consent.

Ethan Wu: Noted. Will add tests that simulate refreshable vs non-refreshable 401 bodies.

Lina Gomez: I'll open the spec PR now with the envelope + mapping table + small migration notes about the new `.retry_after` and `.docs` fields. Please review when ready.

Samir V: Thanks all. Once PRs are up, let's update the onboarding quickstart to show example error handling snippet and a recommended UI pattern (fallback message + link to docs if present).

DevEx Bot: Template reminder: use /templates/error-spec.md in PR description.

Lina Gomez: Linking the ticket: #INFR-2041. Assigning reviewers: @Samir V for node/python, @Ethan Wu for android.

Samir V: I'll land a node patch that wraps responses with Error subclasses (AuthError, RateLimitError, TransientError, ValidationError) and ensure `.retryable` is a property. Will add changelog entry for breaking change to error envelope.

Ethan Wu: I'll add Android mapping + sample app handler to prevent crashes when `.status` is missing. Use safe accessor and surface help link in UI.

QA Bot: Smoke job created and linked to PRs. Will fail build if SDKs return raw strings instead of typed errors.

Lina Gomez: Perfect. Thanks team — hopefully this prevents more demo surprises.
